text: A sample-book made for the Bookly demo. It carries a few calm pages so you can try the w p right away: search, reading-room chat and page citations, all before you index a single book of your own library on this machine. Page 1. The lighthouse keeper climbs the tower every evening and greets the harbour with short flashes of the lamp. Calm weather keeps the lamp glass clean, so the keeper wipes it twic e before sunset. The fog signal always runs one minute before dawn, and sailors say the gentle pattern of light feels like a promise that the shoreline is exactly where the chart promises it to be. On stormy nights the keeper doubles the oil reserve. Page 2. This chapter describes a small reading room beside the harbour with two wooden b and a tall bookshelf filled with poetry volumes and sea charts. A brass kettle warms on the lit tle stove, and paper borrow cards record who took which tale home for the evening. The catalogu e was rebuilt last spring, and the librarian arranged the shelves chronologically so the oldest journal sits at eye level beside the warm window. Page 3. The final page lists the house rules of this sample-book. Keep voices low after nine lls.

lls. Return the borrowed tales before Sunday so the next traveller finds them waiting. Water th e potted fern every third morning with rain collected in the old barrel. And each week write th e favourite quote of the house on the slate board near the door, so visiting sailors leave know ing what the reading room loved most. Page 4. A short appendix collects handy numbers from around the harbour: twelve boats re d for the spring parade, seven poetry volumes on the top shelf, three rainy days last month, an d one friendly dog that guards the pier gate. For demo purposes, ask Bookly a question like how many poetry volumes sit on the top shelf, and it will answer with page numbers.
